title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.7 Helping the Needy

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

People in need are those who lack something necessary, such as food, a pencil or a friend to share with. Matthew 5:42 tells Christians to give to the one who asks and not to turn away from the one who wants to borrow. In this sub-strand you will learn why help matters and practise sharing promptly.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.7: Helping the Needy
Suggested lessons: 2

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.7 Helping the Needy
• Matthew 5:42

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) state the importance of helping the needy
b) demonstrate kindness by sharing with those in need
c) recite Mathew 5:42 and help those in need promptly

## Key inquiry questions
1. How do you help those in need?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• read Matthew 5:42 and tell what they have learnt
• mention instances they helped someone at school, home or in church e.g. they gave a pencil, rubber or shared lunch with another pupil
• role-play sharing items with those who do not have
• write Matthew 5:42 on flash cards and recite it

## Core competencies
• Citizenship: the skill of developing and showing compassion and empathy is portrayed as learners mention instances they helped someone at school, home or in church e.g. they gave a pencil, rubber or shared lunch with another pupil.
• Communication: the skill of writing clearly and correctly is exhibited as learners write Matthew 5:42 on flash cards and recite it.

## Values
• Patriotism: is portrayed as learners demonstrate kindness by sharing with those in need and as they mention instances they helped someone in need.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners read and learn new words.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners role play and sing.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: Why we help people in need

LESSON 1: WHY WE HELP PEOPLE IN NEED
====================================

## What you will learn
• State the importance of helping the needy.
• Demonstrate kindness by sharing with those in need.

Curriculum outcomes: a) state the importance of helping the needy; b) demonstrate kindness by sharing with those in need

## Introduction
A classmate's pencil breaks in the middle of a writing lesson. You have a spare one. That small moment is a chance to help someone in need.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: Why we help people in need — Notes 1

## Notes

The needy are people who lack something they need. A learner may need a pencil, a rubber, lunch, or a friend to walk with. A neighbour may need food or help carrying a load. Helping them is kindness.

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: Why we help people in need — Why help is important

### Why help is important
- Jesus tells His followers to give. Helping obeys Him.
- The person can continue with school or with the day's work.
- Sharing builds friendship and peace.
- You show compassion, which means you feel for the other person and act.
- A class that shares is a kinder community.
- God sees secret kindness as well as public kindness.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: Why we help people in need — Demonstrating kindness

### Demonstrating kindness
Demonstrate means to show by doing. Examples from ordinary days:

- Give a pencil or a rubber to a pupil who has none.
- Share lunch with a classmate who has not brought any.
- Help someone who has fallen to stand up, and call a teacher if they are hurt.
- Help at home when a parent is tired.
- Give in church or at school when there is a proper collection for people in need, with your parent's guidance.

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: Why we help people in need — Notes 4

Do not boast. Do not give something that is not yours to give, such as a sibling's book or school fees. Ask a parent before you give away a large item. Small, honest sharing is already real kindness.

Role-play two pupils. One has no rubber. The other shares and says, "You can use mine." Then swap roles so everyone practises both asking politely and giving gladly. Mention a real time you helped someone at school, at home or in church. Patriotism here includes caring for the people of your own community.

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: Why we help people in need — Stories of help and a role-play

## Key words
• needy — a person who lacks something necessary
• kindness — a helpful action done for someone else
• share — to give part of what you have so that another person can use it

## Activity: Stories of help and a role-play
You will need: A pencil and a rubber for the role-play, Exercise book

1. Mention an instance when you helped someone at school, at home or in church, for example by giving a pencil or a rubber or by sharing lunch.

2. Role-play sharing items with those who do not have them.

3. State why that help was important.

4. Write one kind action you will do this week.

PAGE 10: Lesson 1: Why we help people in need — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Who are the needy?

2. Give two reasons why it is important to help them.

3. Give two ways a Grade 4 learner can share.

## Answers to practice

1. People who lack something they need.

2. Any two: Jesus commands it; it meets a real need; it builds friendship; it shows compassion; God sees kindness.

3. Any two: give a pencil, give a rubber, share lunch, help someone who has fallen, help at home.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: Matthew 5:42: give promptly

## Summary
• The needy lack something necessary.
• Helping them obeys Jesus and shows compassion.
• Share small things honestly, such as a pencil, a rubber or lunch.

LESSON 2: MATTHEW 5:42: GIVE PROMPTLY
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Recite Matthew 5:42.
• Help those in need promptly.

Curriculum outcomes: c) recite Mathew 5:42 and help those in need promptly

## Introduction
Some help arrives too late to be useful. A pencil given after the lesson has ended does not help the writing. Matthew 5:42 calls Christians to give, and the lesson asks us to help promptly.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: Matthew 5:42: give promptly — The two parts

## Notes

Matthew 5:42 says, "Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you."

### The two parts
First, if someone asks for a needed thing that you can rightly give, give it. Second, if someone wants to borrow, do not turn your back. Borrowing means they will use it and it remains yours, such as a rubber for one lesson. Giving can mean they keep it, such as part of your lunch.

Write the verse on a flash card. Recite it until you can say it without looking. Put the card where you will see it before school.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: Matthew 5:42: give promptly — Promptly

### Promptly
Promptly means without unnecessary delay. When you see the need and you can help safely, do it then. Do not wait to be begged three times. Do not laugh first. The widow's son and the lepers met Jesus and He acted. In your small way, act too.

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: Matthew 5:42: give promptly — Wise giving

### Wise giving
- Give what is yours or what a parent has allowed you to share.
- Share school items that do not stop you from doing your own work, or take turns.
- Do not go with a stranger who promises help or gifts.
- Do not give medicine or money you were told to keep.
- If the need is bigger than you, tell a parent, a teacher or a church leader so they can help.
- A polite "I cannot give that, but I will tell a teacher" is better than a lie.

Helping promptly is citizenship in practice: you notice a neighbour's need and you move. Recite Matthew 5:42, then look around the class for one person you can help today.

PAGE 15: Lesson 2: Matthew 5:42: give promptly — Flash cards for Matthew 5:42

## Key words
• promptly — without unnecessary delay
• borrow — to use something that still belongs to the owner and will be returned

## Activity: Flash cards for Matthew 5:42
You will need: Flash cards, Bible, Pens

1. Read Matthew 5:42 and tell what you have learnt.

2. Write the verse on a flash card and recite it.

3. In pairs, one learner asks to borrow a rubber and the other helps promptly.

4. Discuss a need that is too big for a child, and name the adult you would tell.

PAGE 16: Lesson 2: Matthew 5:42: give promptly — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Recite Matthew 5:42.

2. What does promptly mean?

3. A need is bigger than you can meet. What should you do?

## Answers to practice

1. Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.

2. Without unnecessary delay.

3. Tell a parent, a teacher or a church leader so they can help.

PAGE 17: Lesson 2: Matthew 5:42: give promptly — Summary

## Summary
• Matthew 5:42: give to the one who asks, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow.
• Help promptly when the need is one you can meet safely.
• Tell an adult when the need is bigger than you.

PAGE 18: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. The needy are people who...
   A. lack something necessary
   B. always have more than enough
   C. never ask for help
   D. only live in stories

2. Why is it important to help them?

3. Which action demonstrates kindness?
   A. Hiding your extra pencil
   B. Sharing lunch with a classmate who has none
   C. Laughing at a torn book
   D. Taking a friend's rubber by force

4. A learner may share...
   A. a pencil, a rubber or lunch
   B. another child's school fees without asking
   C. medicine meant for someone else
   D. a secret that hides harm

5. Matthew 5:42 says...
   A. turn away from anyone who asks
   B. give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow
   C. lend only to rich people
   D. never share at school

6. To help promptly means...
   A. to wait until next term
   B. to help without unnecessary delay
   C. to help only when a crowd is watching
   D. to refuse and explain later

7. Borrowing means...

8. The need is too big for a child. The right action is:
   A. ignore it
   B. tell a parent, teacher or church leader
   C. go with a stranger who offers money
   D. take someone else's property

9. Boasting after you share...
   A. is the main point of kindness
   B. is not the spirit of quiet help
   C. is required by Matthew 5:42
   D. replaces the gift

10. You have a spare rubber and a classmate asks during the lesson. What should you do?

PAGE 19: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. A. lack something necessary
   A needy person lacks something needed, such as food or a school item.

2. Any one: Jesus tells us to give; it meets a real need; it shows compassion; it builds friendship.
   Helping the needy is both obedience and kindness.

3. B. Sharing lunch with a classmate who has none
   Sharing lunch is one of the examples in this sub-strand.

4. A. a pencil, a rubber or lunch
   Small honest sharing is the kindness Grade 4 learners practise.

5. B. give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow
   That is the verse learners recite.

6. B. to help without unnecessary delay
   Promptly means at the right time, without needless delay.

7. Using something that still belongs to the owner and will be returned.
   Matthew 5:42 speaks about both giving and borrowing.

8. B. tell a parent, teacher or church leader
   Big needs are reported to responsible adults.

9. B. is not the spirit of quiet help
   Kindness does not need boasting.

10. Lend it promptly, because Matthew 5:42 says not to turn away from the one who wants to borrow.
   A small school need can be met at once.
